summary: AstroCare: Mission Health Console is a demo-ready web portal for spaceflight medical oversight. It gives flight surgeons a unified dashboard to monitor crew telemetry across four signal groups—vitals, EVA, radiation, and ECG—alongside clinical context and countermeasure controls. Role-based access separates flight-surgeon and astronaut views, with a pre-filled demo login (surgeon@astrocare.demo) for quick hackathon presentations. The dark, glass-panel UI and clear “DEMO ENVIRONMENT · NOT FOR CLINICAL USE” disclaimer make it safe to showcase. Pitch it as a mission-critical tool that turns raw orbital telemetry into actionable health intelligence for long-duration spaceflight.
details:
AstroCare – Intelligent Astronaut Health Monitoring System

AstroCare is an astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support the health and well-being of astronauts during space missions. Extended space missions expose astronauts to several health risks, including changes in heart rate, oxygen saturation, body temperature, sleep patterns and other physiological conditions.

Our solution aims to provide a centralized monitoring platform that enables continuous observation of astronaut health parameters and helps identify potential health abnormalities.

How It Works

AstroCare provides an interactive dashboard displaying astronaut health information through a human-body visualization and dynamic health indicators. The system processes incoming health measurements, stores relevant information and presents it through an organized interface.

When monitored parameters move outside their defined safe ranges, the platform can generate alerts to help identify potential health concerns.

Key Features

  • Real-time astronaut health monitoring.
  • Interactive human-body visualization.
  • Monitoring of heart rate, oxygen saturation and body temperature.
  • Health status indicators and abnormality alerts.
  • Centralized health information dashboard.
  • Historical health data tracking.
  • Accessible and user-friendly interface.

Technology Stack

Frontend: HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

Backend: Java and Spring Boot.

Database: MySQL and SQL.

Development Tools: Git, GitHub and Visual Studio Code.

Benefits and Intended Impact

AstroCare aims to improve astronaut health awareness, support early identification of abnormal physiological measurements and provide mission teams with organized health information.

The platform is designed with future long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars in mind, where continuous health monitoring will be increasingly important.

Innovation and Creativity

The project combines an interactive astronaut visualization with centralized health monitoring and alert functionality. Its modular architecture is designed to support future integration with wearable sensors, predictive analytics and advanced health-monitoring technologies.

Our team focused on usability, scalability, accessibility and the importance of astronaut safety during long-duration space missions.
